Kelvinlens __VERSION__ — free thermal image viewer, analyser and report tool.

Thermal images and FLIR radiometric video; recalculation with new parameters; spot, area, polygon, line and magic-wand measurements with profiles, formulas and alarms; isotherms, condensation and insulation alarms; automatic hot/cold-spot inspection with severity grading; batch processing, hotspot triage, trends, maps, 3D relief and panoramas; PDF and HTML reports from templates. See the [README](https://github.com/psycho789/kelvinlens#features) for the full list.

## Download

| System | File |
|---|---|
| **Windows** 10/11 (64-bit) | `Kelvinlens_..._x64-setup.exe` (or the `.msi`) |
| **macOS**, Apple Silicon (M1 and later) | `Kelvinlens_..._aarch64.dmg` |
| **macOS**, Intel | `Kelvinlens_..._x64.dmg` |
| **Linux** (any distribution) | `Kelvinlens_..._amd64.AppImage` (`aarch64` for ARM) |
| **Debian / Ubuntu** | `Kelvinlens_..._amd64.deb` |
| **Fedora / openSUSE** | `Kelvinlens-...x86_64.rpm` |

## First launch

The installers are not code-signed yet, so your system will warn you once:

- **macOS:** open the app, click **Done** on the warning, then go to **System Settings → Privacy & Security**, scroll down and click **Open Anyway**. (On macOS 14 and earlier you can instead right-click the app and choose **Open**.)
- **Windows:** on the blue SmartScreen window click **More info → Run anyway**.
- **Linux AppImage:** make it executable (`chmod +x Kelvinlens_*.AppImage`) and run it.

Everything runs offline; Kelvinlens has no network access.
